summary: The main gaps are at the boundary between tool results, persisted surfaces, and the Svelte canvas, plus inconsistent Python/TypeScript execution semantics. The staging plan also needs stronger authorization and environment-safety assertions because initial source execution and existing integration tests do not exercise the same security or service paths.

suggestions.title: Define one canonical linked-surface envelope boundary
suggestions.rationale: `build_linked_surface` returns an inner `CreateSurface`, while `A2UISurface` requires `{version:"v1.0",createSurface}`. `finalize_a2ui_response` inspects output messages but does not extract `a2ui_envelope` from successful tool results, so the handler can forward no usable envelope. Normalize through the existing serialization boundary and test direct output, tool-loop output, and non-A2UI output separately.

suggestions.title: Route linked surfaces through a generic A2UI canvas path
suggestions.rationale: `AgentChat` only creates tabs through `buildInfographicTabData`, whose root check accepts Infographic and Report but rejects the Column, Chart, DataTable, and KPICard roots that the linked builder produces. A real chat test will therefore fail before `A2UISurface` receives the valid envelope. Make the routing contract explicitly support linked-surface roots and test a Column-root tool result with the A2UI feature flag enabled.

suggestions.title: Carry the persisted surface identity with the A2UI artifact and consume refresh responses
suggestions.rationale: `PublishSurfaceTool` returns `surface_id`, but the tab payload has no persisted ID producer, while `A2UISurface` already accepts an optional ID. Its `serverRefresh` posts to the server and discards the response, so successful refreshes cannot update rows, snapshots, or warnings. Define a single artifact metadata shape carrying the envelope and surface ID, pass it through the tab model, and apply the negotiated refresh response to the local data model.

suggestions.title: Authorize source execution before publishing or returning rows
suggestions.rationale: `QuerysourceToolkit.build_linked_surface` executes the source with `pctx=None` and `guard=None`; publishing later invokes guarded persistence, but it cannot revoke rows already returned by the builder. The example tool must either execute with the same owner context and dataplane guard or be explicitly limited to a non-sensitive public dataset, with a test proving an unauthorized source is blocked during initial execution.

suggestions.title: Verify the exact PBAC resource and action used by staging
suggestions.rationale: The guard authorizes `source:query_slug:public:<slug>` with action `source:read`, while the proposed policy name is described as `query_slug:public:epson_*`. That naming difference can make a valid policy appear absent and is indistinguishable from a missing guard if the test only asserts 403. The staging prerequisite should log or assert the effective evaluator resource/action for both allow and deny cases.

suggestions.title: Use one conformance fixture for Python and TypeScript conditions
suggestions.rationale: The TypeScript condition builder emits `limit` and `_offset: 0`, whereas Python omits those fields and adds `querylimit` in the executor. TypeScript `setParam` also accepts undeclared names while Python ignores them. A shared fixture should compare request bodies and ignored-parameter behavior, including locked parameters, instead of testing each implementation independently.

suggestions.title: Make multiquery frame selection identical across lanes
suggestions.rationale: Python raises when a declared `multi_output` is missing or multiple frames are ambiguous. TypeScript instead falls back to `result`, a sole frame, or `[]`, potentially marking a wrong result as ready. Standardize the selector contract so missing or ambiguous frames produce an unavailable/error update while retaining the prior snapshot, then cover all three cases in parity tests.

suggestions.title: Validate FilterBar bindings at envelope validation time
suggestions.rationale: The linked catalog validator checks source graph structure but not a FilterBar's `param.source` and `param.name`. The UI then forwards those values to `setParam`, where an unknown name is currently accepted into overrides. Reject an unknown source or parameter before persistence and add a negative envelope test; keep locked-parameter behavior explicit rather than relying on a silent UI no-op.

suggestions.title: Separate fake integration coverage from a gated staging verdict
suggestions.rationale: The existing server integration tests replace QuerySource, Postgres, catalog, and guard behavior, while the UI tests mock fetch. They verify control flow but cannot prove QS 5.1.2 schemas, real PBAC policy loading, multiquery persistence, share access, or cross-lane parity. Keep those deterministic tests and add a separately gated staging suite that refuses non-staging targets, validates slug definitions before seeding, and asserts the complete HTTP verdict.

suggestions.title: Keep the Epson dashboard tool thin and example-scoped
suggestions.rationale: The core `build_linked_surface` builder already accepts multiple components, sources, and frames, while the public QuerysourceToolkit tool intentionally handles one slug and one component. The Epson tool should compose descriptors, execute through the existing executor, and call the builder without duplicating toolkit validation or becoming a second general-purpose public API. A golden envelope plus one executor trace is sufficient to detect divergence.
